care_profile.owner_says: Very delicate. Will bleach and crisp up if they get too much sun. They need very little water.
care_profile.quirks: Wilts dramatically when thirsty and recovers within hours of watering, so the droop is a free early warning. Far more often killed by overwatering than by drought, so do not water on a schedule.
care_profile.notes: Count unknown; the owner said 'the leafy plants with white flowers and some green flowers'.

care_profile.owner_says: Wild and seems to be okay in any situation. Definitely the heartiest of the group. If it gets too crispy or starts dying, move it away from the sun.
care_profile.notes: Species unknown, which matters: it decides whether this one needs a winter dormancy period.

care_profile.owner_says: Water once every three days or less.
Hard to water normally. Lift the arms of the plant up and pour water directly under the plant, because it is so thick. Once every three days or less.
care_profile.quirks: Foliage is dense enough that water poured on top runs off instead of reaching the soil. Lift the fronds and pour underneath.

care_profile.owner_says: Needs regular water but not a ton at a time.
care_profile.quirks: The only plant in this group asked for CONSISTENT moisture. Its needs are the opposite of the peace lilies, so the two must never share a LetPot dripper line.
care_profile.notes: Giant sequoia is a mountain tree and is likely far more cold hardy than the tropicals here. The 55F threshold is kept until the owner confirms, because guessing wrong costs a plant and guessing right only costs a carried pot.

questions: How many peace lilies are there, and how many vines?
What kind of bonsai is it? It decides whether it needs a winter dormancy period.
Does the sequoia sprout actually need to come in at 55F, or is it hardier than the others?
How old is the sequoia sprout, and has it been through a winter yet?
Is the front porch covered? A covered porch runs a few degrees warmer than open air.
When are you back? It decides whether this is a summer problem or a winter one.
